claims.text: Adding Si to CrFeCoNiX enables formation of a stable, coherent protective oxide layer during high-temperature exposure.
Si segregates to the metal/oxide interface during high-temperature exposure.
Interfacial Si reacts to form a continuous, amorphous, viscous SiO2 layer.
The SiO2 interlayer impedes oxygen diffusion.
The SiO2 interlayer impedes metal-cation diffusion.
The viscous SiO2 interlayer relieves or mitigates interfacial stresses.
Diffusion inhibition and stress mitigation by the SiO2 interlayer prevent oxide-scale cracking and spallation.
Mn-containing CrFeCoNiX alloys form less compliant, polycrystalline oxides rather than a protective SiO2-like interlayer.
Al-containing CrFeCoNiX alloys form less compliant, polycrystalline oxides rather than a protective SiO2-like interlayer.
The oxide scales formed on the Mn- or Al-containing alloys are more stress-prone and susceptible to cracking and spallation.
Under identical exposure conditions above 900 °C, the Si-containing alloy will show less cracking and spallation than the Mn- or Al-containing alloys.
The proposed behavior applies to prolonged exposure of single-phase CrFeCoNiX alloys above 900 °C in oxidative or mildly corrosive atmospheres.
